clippings.speaker: Robert De Niro
clippings.quote: We have known each other for long. And we have a special relationship, I can say. We get together from time to time. We talk about stuff that’s personal, help, give each other advice on things…
clippings.title: Talking With Al Pacino And Robert De Niro: An MW Exclusive
clippings.context: Joint interview with Mayank Shekhar during The Irishman press tour, asked how their relationship had evolved.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: You know, we have been through a lot of the same things. And unusual stuff has happened to us in this profession. We knew each other when we were very young, too. Not well. But we had met. … But I think that even at that time, there was a certain comfort when we’d meet. … And there’s a lot of trust there between us. And love too.
clippings.title: Talking With Al Pacino And Robert De Niro: An MW Exclusive
clippings.context: Same joint interview, answering De Niro on their friendship.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: And Bob saw this project (The Irishman). And he read it … He had the foresight to say there’s something that we can do here. Bob and Marty came together, and we discussed it in LA almost seven to eight years ago.
clippings.title: Talking With Al Pacino And Robert De Niro: An MW Exclusive
clippings.context: Pacino credits De Niro with finding the book behind The Irishman, after their Righteous Kill reunion.

clippings.speaker: Robert De Niro
clippings.quote: This movie went through all the twists and turns. From time to time Al would phone up and say, ‘Is it happening?’
clippings.title: De Niro and Pacino: ‘We are very close... We have known each other a long time’
clippings.context: De Niro to Donald Clarke on The Irishman's long development, in a joint interview with Pacino.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: We have known each other for a long time – since ’68. I think early on in our careers we connected from time to time. Similar things happened to us. Then our lives would take different paths. It was that camaraderie that got us together. We are very close. We don’t see each other very much, but when we do it’s always there...
clippings.title: De Niro and Pacino: ‘We are very close... We have known each other a long time’
clippings.context: Pacino on their 50-year friendship, joint interview for The Irishman.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: We’ve played it before: in the film Heat, we were actually on opposite ends, and in Righteous Kill we were close, and in this film we were close in a different way. It came relatively easy to come to that place. I don’t even think we talked about it consciously, but it was in the writing, of course. And in the nature of the two people’s relationship in real life, too.
clippings.title: De Niro and Pacino on The Irishman and the gangsterization of US politics
clippings.context: London audience with both actors, on the Sheeran-Hoffa relationship and their past pairings.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: He’s so great, and he was smart because he said he didn’t want to rehearse the scene with me. He didn’t want to rehearse it. And at first I [had doubts about that]. But then I realized he was right. It really made a difference and that was very clever.
clippings.title: 'Heat' at 25: How Al Pacino hurt himself running away from Robert De Niro
clippings.context: From Yahoo's own 2017 Role Recall interview, on the Heat diner scene; brackets are Yahoo's.

notes: De Niro rarely speaks about Pacino at length; his side is thinner (2 quotes). Variety and Deadline (Heat Academy Q&A) redirect to tollbit and were skipped; Guardian piece only found on PressReader.
